Scene: a festive beach at sunset, the same beach as in the key art. Pale warm sand with soft brushed ripples and low dunes topped with tufts of beach grass. A calm teal sea along the back with thin white foam lines and a ladder of pale golden glints under the sun. A sunset sky that shades from soft rose at the top through peach to pale gold at the horizon, with one low pale sun in a soft glow and long two-tone clouds, cream on top and rose underneath. Low mauve hills far away on the horizon, one tiny white sailboat, and palm trees at the far sides of the beach. Strings of small triangular pennants (coral, teal, yellow, blue, pink and cream) hang on thin wooden poles right across the back of the beach, in exactly the places the source shows; they never move. Warm low golden light with soft long shadows, so the beach has depth and glow. A few small shells and coral starfish lie on the sand where the source shows them. Across the foreground at the start hangs one long cream cloth banner with coral-red edges on two tall wooden poles. BANNER RULE: the banner is completely BLANK cream cloth in every frame, with no writing. One round clock stands on a wooden post in the sand: a plain white clock face in a wooden rim, with two dark hands and NO numbers. Under it on the post hangs one small cream board in a coral-red frame. BOARD RULE: every cream board is completely BLANK in every frame, plain cream with no writing. One wooden notice board stands on two wooden legs in the sand, with one sheet of cream paper pinned on it. PAPER RULE: the cream paper is completely BLANK in every frame: plain cream, with no drawing, no marks and no writing. Far in the background at the left: three more plain Sols stand in a row in front of a tall finished sandcastle with a small blue flag, passing ONE small blue bucket along the row from one to the next, exactly as the source shows. They stay small and far away. The sandcastle is only begun: ONE finished round sand tower with a toothed top and one small dark window, a short piece of sand wall beside it, and one low rounded heap of sand. It is the same in every frame and never changes or grows. One red toy bucket stands upright on the sand beside the castle and one red toy shovel lies on the sand near it. OUR SOL is the plain one, wearing nothing.

His eyes are two navy half-rings with white centres, each cut flat across its top and slanted down toward the middle of his face. He stands at the tower and bobs down three times, at 0.3, 0.8 and 1.3 seconds. 3. At 1.7 seconds he scurries to the right on his tiny feet to the red bucket and bumps it with his side at 2.1 seconds: the bucket rocks once and settles upright. 4. He scurries left to the sand wall (2.55 to 2.9), bobs twice, scurries left to the tower (3.3 to 3.6), bobs, back to the wall, back to the tower, faster each time. From 3.3 seconds his eyes are two round navy rings with white centres and three small pale blue drops fly off above him. 5. At 4.75 seconds he stops in the middle, facing the camera. At 4.8 seconds the drops are gone; he sags down and forward with his arm nubs hanging, his eyes become two small navy curved lines, like gently closed eyes, and one small pale lilac puff floats beside him. 6. At 5.8 seconds the puff is gone and his eyes are two navy ovals again; he tilts back and looks up toward the camera, still sagging a little. 7. At 7.35 seconds he nods once, slowly. ARM RULE: arm nubs stay the same short stubs in every frame; nobody reaches for or holds anything.
